motion.name: ease-out-expo
motion.purpose: Easing for the print sweep, stamp thunk and rise.

motion.name: print-sweep
motion.value: 520ms ease-out-expo; gold rgb(255 204 0 / 0.6) wash grows left to right (background-size 0% to 100%)
motion.purpose: A new entry being printed into the book: fresh import rows (first 24) and a newly saved work card.

motion.name: print-stagger
motion.purpose: Each cell continues the sweep where its neighbour ended; rows cascade downward.

motion.name: print-fade
motion.value: 2200ms ease-out after a 900ms hold (plus stagger); gold alpha 0.6 to 0 via the registered --ink property
motion.purpose: The ink settles after printing. The fresh flag clears after 4500ms.

motion.name: stamp-thunk
motion.value: 420ms ease-out-expo; rotate(-9deg) scale(1.35), then rotate(-1deg) scale(0.96) at 60%, then rotate(-2deg) scale(1)
motion.purpose: A date stamp landing when the date it shows changes.

motion.name: rise
motion.purpose: Toasts and the compose form entering.

motion.name: state
motion.purpose: Button, chip and field colour/border transitions; buttons press down 1px on active.

motion.name: reduced-motion
motion.value: animations and transitions collapse to 1ms with no delay

narrative.overview:
The app is built as a Thai bank passbook (สมุดบัญชี) kept for one business. A deep blue cover runs down the left edge; the pages are a pale, cool grey; every piece of work and every stock import is an entry written into a white leaf and dated with a blue ink stamp. Stock carries a running balance column the way a passbook does. Trust comes from reconciliation, not decoration: a strip under the heading says whether the totals match the source file, and the same totals carry through to the screen, the printout and the Excel file.

Density is that of a desk ledger: one reading size (15px) for everything you scan, tabular numerals everywhere, hairline seams between rows and a single soft shadow under each leaf. Hierarchy comes from weight and colour, not from size jumps. Gold is rationed to the thing in your hand at this moment, so it always answers "where am I / what did I just do". Motion has one job: an entry being "printed" into the book (a gold sweep across a new row) and a date stamp landing with a small thunk.

The world rejects the default admin dashboard: no KPI tiles floating over a white table, no gradient headers, no decorative colour. Summaries are ruled lines or one divided strip; tables carry a solid blue header band.
keyCharacteristics: 60/30/10 colour: cool grey page, deep blue cover, gold for the thing in hand.
Two Thai voices: looped Noto Sans Thai Looped for titles and stamps, Anuphan for everything read or typed.
One data size (15px) with tabular figures; hierarchy by weight.
White leaves (10px corners) with 1px seams on a flat grey page.
Blue ink date stamps, tilted, on every dated heading.
The "print" sweep for new entries; state recolours rows in place.
Thai-first copy, Buddhist-era dates, Thai unit nouns on every count.

rules.name: The 60/30/10 Rule
rules.body: Ledger Grey about 60% of any screen, blue about 30% (the rail plus header bands, primary actions and selections), gold no more than 10%. The rule is pinned by the owner (#EAEFEF / #005A9C / #FFCC00) and holds in screen, print, Excel and the favicon alike.

rules.name: The Thing-In-Hand Rule
rules.body: Pure gold marks only what the user is holding right now: the active tab's count, the selected import, the card being written or edited, the sorted column's arrow, the rows that just arrived, the toast that just appeared, the file being dragged. Nothing at rest is gold except the seal, which is the book's mark. If two things on one screen are gold for different reasons, one of them is wrong.

rules.name: The Used-Phone Tint Rule
rules.body: มือ 2 is always told apart by blue before its label is read: on screen it is a solid Passbook Blue badge with Cover Paper text, while มือ 1 sits on Leaf Wash in ink; in print and Excel the whole มือ 2 row carries Used-Phone Wash.

rules.name: The One Data Size Rule
rules.body: Every figure in a table, list or meta line sits at body size with tabular numerals. Quantities and brands rise by weight (600) and colour (Blue Ink), never by size. The strip's 24px figures are the single exception, because they are the verdict.

rules.name: The Two Voices Rule
rules.body: Noto Sans Thai Looped is for what the book prints (titles, heads, stamps, wordmark). Anything the user reads row by row or types is Anuphan.

rules.name: The Thai-First Rule
rules.body: All UI copy is Thai. Dates use the Buddhist era: "22 พ.ย. 69" on stamps and in the UI, "22/11/69" in export titles. Numbers use Thai thousands separators. Every count carries its Thai unit noun (เครื่อง, รายการ, รุ่น, บรรทัด, การ์ด). Latin appears only for file formats and for product data carried over from the source report.

rules.name: The Leaf-On-Page Rule
rules.body: There is one surface level. If something needs to stand out, it gets a gold ring or a blue fill, not a bigger shadow.

rules.name: The Ink Stamp Rule
rules.body: Every dated heading carries a Blue Ink stamp (Buddhist era, -2deg tilt, uneven ink); it lands with the stamp thunk when its date changes.

rules.name: The Header Band Rule
rules.body: Every ledger table header is a solid Passbook Blue band with light 600 labels, on screen, in print and in Excel; totals close with a 2px Blue Ink rule over a grey row.

rules.name: The Isolated Delete Rule
rules.body: Delete is an outline icon set apart by a seam divider; the first press becomes a solid ยืนยันลบ that holds focus, and blur reverts it. No modal.

rules.name: The Print Rule
rules.body: New entries arrive as a gold sweep left to right across the row, then the ink fades; state changes recolour rows in place without moving the grid.

rules.name: The No-Tiles Rule
rules.body: Summaries are one divided strip or one ruled line, never a row of separate KPI tiles.

dos: Do keep the 60/30/10 split: Ledger Grey page (#EAEFEF), Passbook Blue cover, header bands and selections (#005A9C), gold (#FFCC00) under 10%.
Do use Passbook Blue (cover) for fills with Cover Paper text, and Blue Ink (cover-deep) for blue text and lines on light grounds, even while they share a value.

Do reserve pure gold for the thing in hand: the active count, the selected import, the card being written, the sorted column, rows that just arrived; on blue, the seal, the active sort arrow, the toast icon and the rail focus ring.
Do date every dated heading with a Blue Ink stamp, Buddhist era, tilted -2deg.
Do set every table, list and meta figure at 15px with tabular numerals and build hierarchy with weight (600) and Blue Ink, not size.
Do give every ledger table the solid blue header band and close totals with a 2px Blue Ink rule over a grey row, on screen, in print and in Excel.
Do mark มือ 2 in blue everywhere: the solid badge on screen, the Used-Phone Wash row in print and Excel.
Do make delete an outline icon set apart by a seam divider, confirmed in place by a solid red ยืนยันลบ that holds focus.
Do announce new entries with the print sweep and recolour state changes in place without moving the grid.
Do write every label in Thai, with Thai unit nouns on counts and Buddhist-era dates.
Do put content on 10px Leaf White leaves with a 1px seam and the single leaf shadow.
donts: Don't build summaries as KPI tiles; use the divided strip or a ruled balance line.
Don't use gold as a button fill, heading colour, background or decoration.
Don't raise a number's size to make it important; the strip figures are the only 24px numerals.
Don't add elevation levels or hover lifts to leaves; stand things out with a gold ring or blue fill.
Don't confirm deletes with a modal, or place the delete button flush against edit without a divider.
Don't set body text, data or form input in Noto Sans Thai Looped; it is for titles, heads and stamps.
Don't write Gregorian dates or untranslated English labels in the UI.
Don't extend Gold Wash to new persistent states; it belongs to rows and targets being acted on.
